I'll help you get set up. First, let me gather a bit more information so I can give you the right checklist.

Packaged zobo drinks fall under the DRINKS category, and Ibadan is in Oyo State. To build your plan, I need to know:

**Is your business already registered with CAC** (the Corporate Affairs Commission)? That's the business registration authority in Nigeria, and it decides where you start.

Here's your checklist for starting your zobo business in Ibadan. The steps follow the order the regulators require, and I've grouped them into stages so you can see what comes first.

## Start here (before you register anything)

1. **Check your product meets NAFDAC's fruit juice rules** [1] — NAFDAC sets the standards for what can go into packaged zobo. Make sure your recipe and ingredients comply before you move forward.

2. **CAC business name registration** [2] — Register your business name with the Corporate Affairs Commission. This is your foundation; most other registrations depend on it.

3. **Trademark availability search** [3] — Search to make sure your brand name isn't already taken. This is quick and inexpensive, and you need to do it before you file the trademark application.

## Once your CAC registration comes through

4. **Your production facility meets NAFDAC requirements** [1] — NAFDAC will inspect where you make the drinks. Your facility needs to be clean, properly equipped, and meet their hygiene standards.

5. **Federal Tax ID** [6] — Register with the Nigeria Revenue Service to get your tax ID number.

6. **Oyo State tax registration** [6] — Register with Oyo State's tax authority.

7. **Food handler medical tests** [1] — You and anyone else making the drinks need medical clearance (health tests). This is ongoing; you'll need to renew it regularly.

8. **Trademark application (filing)** [3] — File your trademark with the Intellectual Property Office.

## Before you can sell

9. **NAFDAC facility inspection application and inspection** [1] — Once your facility is ready and your staff have medical clearance, apply for NAFDAC to inspect it. They'll check everything before you can register your product.

10. **Laboratory analysis of your samples** [1] — NAFDAC will test samples of your zobo to confirm it meets the fruit juice standards.

11. **NAFDAC product registration** [1] — This is the key approval. NAFDAC registers your specific product so you can legally sell it.

12. **Product labelling** [1] — Your bottles must have labels that meet NAFDAC's requirements (ingredients, allergens, expiry date, etc.).

13. **Trademark examination and acceptance** [3] — The Intellectual Property Office examines your trademark application.

14. **Trademark publication and opposition period** [3] — Your trademark is published; others have time to object if they think it conflicts with theirs.

15. **Trademark registration certificate** [3] — Once the opposition period passes, you get your trademark certificate.

16. **Oyo State business premises registration** [7] — Register your production premises with Oyo State's Ministry of Trade, Industry, Investment and Cooperatives.

## Every year

17. **CAC annual returns** [2] — File your annual return with CAC.

18. **Oyo State business premises renewal** [7] — Renew your premises registration.

19. **NAFDAC product registration renewal** [1] — Renew your product registration.

20. **Trademark renewal** [3] — Renew your trademark registration.

The order matters because NAFDAC won't inspect your facility until you have a CAC registration and your staff have medical clearance, and they won't register your product until the facility inspection and lab tests are done. Similarly, you can't file your trademark application until you've searched for conflicts.

Would you like me to go through any of these steps in more detail, or do you have questions about fees, timelines, or what documents you'll need?

**Sources**

1. NAFDAC requirements for packaged fruit drinks made in Nigeria (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [nafdac.gov.ng](https://nafdac.gov.ng/food/guideline-for-micro-scale-enterprises/)
2. Business registration with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [www.cac.gov.ng](https://www.cac.gov.ng/services/business-name)
3. Trademark registration — Trademarks, Patents and Designs Registry (Nigerian Intellectual Property Office) (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [nipo.gov.ng](https://nipo.gov.ng/trademark.jsp)
4. Data protection requirements for businesses that collect customers' personal data — Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [ndpc.gov.ng](https://ndpc.gov.ng/dpco-registration-requirements/)
5. Product certification for locally made products — Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) MANCAP (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [son.gov.ng](https://son.gov.ng/mancapservice/)
6. Tax registration — federal (Nigeria Revenue Service) and state internal revenue services (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [www.nrs.gov.ng](https://www.nrs.gov.ng/)
7. State business premises permits — Oyo, Lagos, FCT, Rivers, Ogun and Edo (information as of 25 Oct 2026) · [trade.oyostate.gov.ng](https://trade.oyostate.gov.ng/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/PROCEDURES-FOR-REGISTRATION-OF-BUSINESS-PREMISES.pdf)

Registering a business name with CAC costs **₦10,000** and officially takes **24 working hours** [1]. That fee includes certified copies of your registration documents.

Before you register, you'll need to reserve your chosen name for ₦500, which takes about 4 working hours [1]. The reservation is valid for 60 days, so you have that long to complete the full registration.

You can do the whole process online through the CAC's Company Registration Portal at https://icrp.cac.gov.ng/. You'll need to upload your NIN (or passport, driver's licence or voter's card), a passport photograph, your signature, and details about your business and residential address [1].

Keep in mind that CAC can change these fees and timelines, so confirm the current amounts on cac.gov.ng before you pay.

**Sources**

1. Business registration with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) — Business name registration — sole proprietorship (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [cac.gov.ng](https://www.cac.gov.ng/services/business-name)

Great! Now that your CAC registration is done, here's what comes next for your drinks business in Oyo. The steps are grouped by stage so you can see the flow.

**Start here (ready now)**

1. **Check your product composition meets NAFDAC's Fruit Juice and Nectar Regulations** [1] — NAFDAC won't register your drink unless it meets their standards for juice content, additives and other requirements.

2. **Search for trademark availability** [2] — Before you file for your brand name, you need to check that no one else has already registered it.

3. **Confirm whether your product needs MANCAP certification** [3] — This is optional but recommended. It's a quality mark from SON (Standards Organisation of Nigeria) that shows your product meets Nigerian standards.

4. **Make sure your production facility meets NAFDAC requirements** [1] — Your premises must have proper hygiene, equipment and layout. NAFDAC will inspect this later.

5. **Get your Federal Tax ID** [4] — You'll need this from the Nigeria Revenue Service before you can apply for state tax registration or NAFDAC inspection.

6. **Register with Oyo State tax authority** [4] — Once you have your Federal Tax ID, register with Oyo State Internal Revenue Service.

7. **Get medical tests for your production staff** [1] — Food handlers must have health certificates. This is required and recurring (you'll need to renew them).

**Once the above are done**

The next steps follow in order: file your trademark application, apply for NAFDAC facility inspection, get lab analysis of your product samples, then finally NAFDAC product registration. After that comes product labelling, and then you can start selling.

You'll also need to register your business premises with Oyo State once your state tax registration is complete.
